","complete":true},"stderr":{"text":"","complete":true}}],"artifacts":[{"path":"artifacts/report.md","role":"produced","sha256":"015b33f19af708aff0c3aea5db43350c9cd5c2f48e609ccbd56d7953f3bbc840","bytes":2629,"content":"# Fact Check

## Claim

The Great Wall of China is visible from space with the naked eye.

**Verdict:** refuted

**Confidence:** 0.97

## Summary

Multiple authoritative sources, including NASA and astronaut accounts, state the Great Wall of China is generally not visible from space with the unaided eye; it is difficult or impossible to see from low Earth orbit without magnification and certainly not from the Moon.

## Evidence

- **NASA** (https://www.nasa.gov/image-article/great-wall/): Despite myths to the contrary, the wall isn't visible from the moon, and is difficult or impossible to see from Earth orbit without the high-powered lenses used for this photo.
- **NASA (China's Wall Less Great in View from Space)** (https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/static/history/PDFs/great_wall_less_great_from_space.pdf): The Great Wall of China, frequently billed as the only man-made object visible from space, generally isn't, at least to the unaided eye in low Earth orbit. It certainly isn't visible from the Moon; NASA's Kamlesh Lulla says it is very, very difficult to distinguish in astronaut photography.
- **Scientific American** (https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/no-you-cant-see-the-great-wall-of-china-from-space/): The wall is too narrow to resolve by eye even from low Earth orbit (~0.1 arcminute width), and astronauts have never reliably seen it unaided; China's first taikonaut Yang Liwei said he couldn't see it from orbit.
- **ESA** (https://www.esa.int/ESA_Multimedia/Images/2018/06/Great_Wall_of_China): ESA astronaut Alexander Gerst: 'Can we see the Great Wall of China from the ISS? Next to impossible with the naked eye. But I tried with an 800 mm tele lens. Still tough to spot.'
- **PMC (López-Gil, 'Is it Really Possible to See the Great Wall of China from Space with a Naked Eye?')** (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3972694/): Optical analysis concludes not even the best human eye could see the Great Wall from space; the relevant parameter is the wall's width (usually under 6 m), making it impossible at a glance.
- **BBC Sky at Night Magazine** (https://www.skyatnightmagazine.com/space-science/can-you-see-great-wall-china-from-space): The truth is that the Great Wall of China cannot be seen from space with the naked eye; it can only be photographed or observed using magnification.
- **Encyclopaedia Britannica** (https://www.britannica.com/question/Can-you-see-the-Great-Wall-of-China-from-space): You typically can't see the Great Wall of China from space; the popular claim was disproved when astronauts stated it was not visible with the naked eye from the Moon.
